Rashi on Niddah 26b:10:1.hebrew: באלי ואתי - שהיה ממהר לבא, כמו (לעיל נדה דף יז.) באלי דידבי, פי' מגרש:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:10:1.english: Ba'alei va'atei [hurrying and coming] - [This means] that he was hurrying to come, like (above, Niddah 17a) "ba'alei didevei," meaning "drives away."

Rashi on Niddah 26b:10:2.english: Of D’vil - The name of a place.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:10:3.english: With a straw of wheat - That is to say, with a few questions.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:10:4.english: He falls and is pushed away - That is to say, to challenge him and refute him, so that he will not know [how] to reply.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:11:1.hebrew: אלא בדבר של קיימא - שכיוצא בו מתקיים אם היום היו חדשיו כלו, למעוטי שאם הפילה דבר שאין ראוי לבריית נשמה — כגון בירך אחד באמצע, או גוף אטום, או מפלת מין בהמה וחיה ועוף — ואח"כ הפילה שליא, אפי' בתוך ג' ימים, חוששת לולד אחר:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:11:1.english: Only to a viable item - [Meaning, something] whose like survives if its months were completed today; to exclude [a case] where she miscarried something that is not fit for the creation of a soul — such as [one] with one thigh in the middle, or a sealed body, or [if] she miscarries a species of domesticated animal, wild animal, or bird — and afterward she miscarries an afterbirth, even within three [days], she must be concerned about another fetus.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:11:2.english: He looked at Rav Yehuda harshly - Because he [Rav Yehuda] had heard it and did not tell it to him [Shmuel].

Rashi on Niddah 26b:12:1.hebrew: המפלת עורב ושליא מהו - מי תלינן שליא בעורב ולא ניחוש לולד אחר, או לא תלינן:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:12:1.english: She who discharges a crow and an afterbirth, what is [the halakha] - Do we attribute the afterbirth to the crow and not be concerned about another fetus, or do we not attribute [it]?

Rashi on Niddah 26b:12:2.hebrew: שיש במינו - כגון אדם ובהמה וחיה, אבל עוף לא:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:12:2.english: Whose species has [an afterbirth] - Such as a human, a domesticated animal, or a wild animal; however, a bird [does] not.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:1:1.english: Girls' ovens - Young girls make ovens to play [with].

Rashi on Niddah 26b:1:2.hebrew: תחלתו ארבעה - תנור בן ד' טפחים מקבל טומאה, אם נגמרה מלאכתו:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:1:2.english: Its beginning [is] four - An oven of four handbreadths [in height] is susceptible to ritual impurity if its manufacture is completed.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:1:3.hebrew: ושיריו ד' - נטמא תנור גדול ושברו, ונשתיירו ד' טפחים, עדיין טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:1:3.english: And its remains [are] four [handbreadths] - [If] a large oven became impure and one broke it, and four handbreadths remained, it is still impure.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:2:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: תחלתו כל שהוא משתגמר מלאכתו ושיריו ברובו, ומקשה בהעור והרוטב: רובו דטפח למאי חזי? ומשני: האי "ושיריו" אגדול קאי, <abbr title="והכי קאמר">וה"ק</abbr>: שירי גדול ברובו. ומותבינן: בגדול והא קאמר שיריו <abbr title="ארבעה">ד'</abbr>? ומשנינן: ההוא בתנור בר <abbr title="שבעה">ז'</abbr>, <abbr title="דארבעה">דד'</abbr> הוי רובו, והא בתנור בר <abbr title="תשעה">ט'</abbr>:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:2:1.english: This is the reading: "[In] its original state, any size, once its construction is completed, and its remains [must be] the majority of it." And [the Gemara] raises a difficulty in [the chapter] Ha'or Veharotev: What is the majority of a handbreadth fit for? And it answers: This [phrase] "and its remains" refers to the large [oven], and this is what it is saying: the remains of a large [oven] [must be] the majority of it. And we raise an objection: Regarding a large [oven], did it not say its remains [are] four [handbreadths]? And we answer: That [statement refers] to an oven of seven [handbreadths], for four is its majority, whereas this [statement refers] to an oven of nine [handbreadths].

Rashi on Niddah 26b:3:1.hebrew: בפלוגתא - כגון הכא, דלר"מ לא הוי שיעורא בטפח:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:3:1.english: In a dispute - Such as here, where according to Rabbi Meir, the [minimum] measure is not a handbreadth.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:4:1.hebrew: לא אמרו טפח אלא בין תנור ולכותל - דהתם יותר מטפח עומדת ליקצץ, מפני שמעכב את התנור מלקרבו לכותל ודוחקת את הכותל. הילכך, יותר מטפח עומדת לינטל היא, אבל לצד הבית, אפי' גדולה הרבה, יד הוא לתנור:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:4:1.english: They said a handbreadth only between [the] oven and the wall - For there, [a stone protruding] more than a handbreadth stands to be cut off, because it prevents the oven from being brought close to the wall and presses against the wall. Therefore, [if it protrudes] more than a handbreadth, it stands to be removed; but toward the side of the house, even [if it is] very large, it is a handle for the oven.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:5:1.english: With [matters] that are written - Whose measure is explicitly stated in the Torah.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:6:1.english: It is enough for a [cross] beam - With regard to an alleyway.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:6:2.english: Of rabbinic law - Such as an alleyway, for its entire precept is from the words of the Scribes.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:1.hebrew: כל ג' ימים - כגון יצא ולד תחלה ושליא אחריו בתוך ג' ימים:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:1.english: All three days - For example, [where] an offspring emerged first, and an afterbirth [emerged] after it within three days.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:2.hebrew: תולין השליא - בו ואין חוששין לאחר, דתוך הזמן הזה עשויה השליא להתעכב אחר הולד שהיתה ממנו, טפי לא. ואם זה זכר, תשב לזכר בלבד, ולא אמרינן שליא אחרת היתה עם ולד זה ונימוח, ושליא זו דולד אחר היא, דדרך שליא לשהות אחר ולד ג' ימים:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:2.english: We attribute the afterbirth - to it [the offspring], and we are not concerned about another [offspring], for within this time the afterbirth is apt to be delayed after the offspring from which it came; longer [than that, it does] not. And if this [offspring] is a male, she observes [the days] for a male alone, and we do not say [that] another afterbirth was with this offspring and [its offspring] dissolved, and [that] this afterbirth belongs to another offspring, for it is the way of an afterbirth to tarry after an offspring [for] three days.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:3.hebrew: מכאן ואילך חוששין - שמא ולד אחר היה עמו, ונקבה היה, ותשב ימי טומאה דנקבה. ואי נמי הוי האי ולד נקבה, אכתי מהניא ספק דשליא, דמנינא ימי טוהר לחומרא, שאם תראה ליום פ"א לולד ופסקה עד יום שמיני וראתה, לא הויא שומרת יום כנגד יום, (דאמר בהדיא) שליא נקבה הואי, ומה שראתה ביום פ"א דם טוהר הוה, דמשליא מנינן, והשתא הוא דהויא תחלת נדה, והיא נקראת טועה:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:7:3.english: From this [point] forward, we are concerned - lest another offspring was with it, and it was a female, so she must observe the days of impurity for a female [birth]. And even if this [first] offspring was a female, the doubt regarding the afterbirth still has an effect, in that we count the days of purity stringently: for if she sees [blood] on the eighty-first day from [the birth of] the offspring, and ceases until the eighth day [thereafter] and sees [blood], she is not [certainly] a woman who observes a day against a day, (for one says explicitly) the afterbirth was a female, and what she saw on the eighty-first day was pure blood, since we count from the afterbirth, and now is when it is the beginning of niddah; and she is called a confused woman [to'ah].

Rashi on Niddah 26b:8:1.english: In [the case of] non-viable newborns - [the second offspring] lingers.

Rashi on Niddah 26b:9:1.hebrew: את אמרת לשמעתתיה דרב - בתמיה. כלומר, את אתית לפרושי מדידך:
Rashi on Niddah 26b:9:1.english: You say Rav’s teaching - [This is said] as a question. That is to say, did you come to explain [it] on your own?

Rashi on Niddah 26b:9:3.english: She gave birth - [To] a viable child.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:13:1.hebrew: המפלת חיה ועוף כו' - דוקא נקט חיה ועוף, דאי בתחלה ולד ואח"כ שליא, עד ג' ימים תולין ואין חוששין לולד אחר. ולכאורה נראה הטעם: דחיה ועוף אין דרכן של נשים להפיל, ולכך איכא לספוקי שהשליא אינה מהם. וקשה: דבפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עז:) אהא דתנן: "שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה", ומסיק אר"א: "לא שנו אלא שאינה קשורה בולד" — פי': שיש לה ולד אחר, וכיון דאינה קשורה בו חוששין לולד אחר בשליא, ולכך אסורה — ומייתי: "תניא נמי הכי" מהך ד"המפלת חיה ועוף". והיכי מייתי? הא אדרבה, משמע הכא דוקא חיה ועוף דלאו אורחיה, אבל נפל דאורחיה — תולין כל שלשה ימים, ובבן קיימא — אפי' כמה ימים! וי"ל: דאין הדבר תלוי באורחיה ולא אורחיה, אלא קים ליה להש"ס דאמר צורת אדם רגילה השליא להתעכב, אבל לאחר בהמה חיה ועוף אינה רגילה להפרד השליא מן הולד אפי' במעי הבהמה, כמו במעי האשה. וא"ת: וכי אינה קשורה בולד, אמאי קאמר ר"א דאסורה באכילה? הא אמרינן הכא דלא הוי אלא ספק ולא ודאי ולד אחר, מדקתני: "הריני מטיל עליה חומר שני ולדות", שמא נימוח שפיר של שליא זו; וא"כ הוי ספק ספקא: דלמא אין כאן ולד אחר, ואפי' איכא — שמא לא יצא לא ראשו ולא רובו! ובפ"ק דב"ק (דף יא.) גבי שליא שיצתה מקצתה ביום ראשון משמע דספק ספקא שרי, דפריך: "מאי קמ"'ל? דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד? תנינא: שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה!" — פי': ואם יש מקצת שליא בלא ולד, הוה ליה ספק ספקא ושרי. וי"ל: דברייתא דקתני "שמא" איירי בשליא שאחר הולד, ור"א איירי בשליא שיצתה קודם הולד, דודאי יש שם ולד אחר כשאינה קשורה בו, כדאמרינן בשמעתין: "לא אמרו תולין השליא בולד אלא בשליא שבאה אחר הולד". והתם מייתי ראיה דבאינה קשורה חוששין לולד אחר, לאפוקי מדר' יוחנן דהתם. אי נמי: אפילו בספק ספקא אסרה ר"א, דגזרינן מקצתה אטו רובה, או אטו אין עמה ולד אחר — דיטעו העולם ויסברו הא דשרינן מה שבפנים לאו משום ספק ספקא, אלא משום "כל בבהמה", וגזרת הכתוב הוא דאפי' יצא רובו שרי מיעוטו שבפנים; כיון דחזו דשרינן ביצתה מקצתה, ואפשר דיצא הראש באותו מקצת והוי כיוצא רובו, ולא יעלו על לבם דמשום ספק ספקא שרי:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:13:1.english: [A woman] who discharges [a type of] undomesticated animal, or bird, etc. - [The baraita] specifically stated "undomesticated animal or bird," for if first [there is] an offspring and afterward an afterbirth, up to three days we attribute [the afterbirth to the offspring] and are not concerned about another offspring. And seemingly the reason appears [to be] that it is not usual for women to miscarry an undomesticated animal or bird, and therefore there is room to doubt that the afterbirth is not from them. And [this is] difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMakshah (Chullin 77b), on that which we learned in the Mishnah: "An afterbirth that emerged partially is forbidden to be eaten," and [the Gemara] concludes: Rabbi Elazar said: "They only taught [that it is forbidden] when it is not tied to an offspring" — meaning, that it has another offspring, and since it is not tied to it, we are concerned about another offspring in the afterbirth, and therefore it is forbidden — and [the Gemara] brings [a proof]: "It was also taught thus [in a baraita]" from this [baraita] of "[A woman] who discharges an undomesticated animal or bird." But how does it bring [a proof from here]? On the contrary, it is implied here [that] specifically [with] an undomesticated animal or bird, which is not its normal way, [do we not attribute the afterbirth to it], whereas [with] a stillborn, which is its normal way, we attribute [the afterbirth to it] all three days, and with a viable child even several days! And one can answer: that the matter does not depend on "its normal way" or "not its normal way"; rather, it was established to the Talmud that [after] a human form the afterbirth tends to be delayed, whereas after an [offspring in the form of] a domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird, the afterbirth does not tend to separate from the offspring, even in the womb of an animal just as in the womb of a woman. And if you ask: when it is not tied to the offspring, why did Rabbi Elazar say that it is forbidden to be eaten? Behold, we say here that it is only a doubt and not definitely another offspring, as it teaches: "I impose upon her the stringency of two offspring," [because] perhaps the amniotic sac of this afterbirth dissolved! And if so, it is a double doubt (sefek sefeika): perhaps there is no other offspring here, and even if there is, perhaps neither its head nor its majority emerged! And in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (11a), regarding an afterbirth that emerged partially on the first day, it is implied that a double doubt is permitted, for [the Gemara] asks: "What does he teach us? That there is no partial afterbirth without an offspring? We [already] learned [this in a Mishnah]: 'An afterbirth that emerged partially is forbidden!'" — meaning: and if there is a partial afterbirth without an offspring, it would be a double doubt and permitted. And one can answer: that the baraita that teaches "perhaps" [i.e., a doubt] deals with an afterbirth that [comes] after the offspring, whereas Rabbi Elazar deals with an afterbirth that emerged before the offspring, where there is definitely another offspring there when it is not tied to it, as we say in our sugya: "They only said we attribute the afterbirth to the offspring when the afterbirth came after the offspring." And there [in Chullin], [the Gemara] brings a proof that when it is not tied we are concerned about another offspring, to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Yochanan there. Alternatively: even in a double doubt, Rabbi Elazar forbade it, because we decree [regarding] its partial [emergence] on account of [a case of] its majority, or on account of [a case where] there is no other offspring with it — lest people err and think that what we permit inside is not because of a double doubt, but because of "whatever is in the animal" [i.e., the verse permitting what is inside a slaughtered animal], and it is a scriptural decree that even if its majority emerged, its minority that is inside is permitted — since they see that we permit [it] when its [afterbirth] emerged partially, and it is possible that the head emerged in that partial [emergence] and it is like its majority emerging, and it will not enter their minds that it is permitted because of a double doubt:

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:2:1.hebrew: אבל בקטן תחלתו כל שהוא - וא"ת: וגדול שאין לו ד' טפחים, אמאי טהור? והלא אף בקטן טפי, טמא? וי"ל דגדול וקטן היינו ברוחב; והרוחב הרבה צריך גובה ד' להחזיק חומו, אבל קטן שהוא צר, די בגובה טפח:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:2:1.english: But with regard to a small [oven], its original state [is] any size - And if you ask: Why is a large [oven] that does not have four handbreadths [in height] pure? Is it not impure even when it is smaller? One can answer that "large" and "small" refer to the width: one that is very wide requires a height of four [handbreadths] to retain its heat, whereas for a small [oven], which is narrow, a height of one handbreadth suffices.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:2:2.hebrew: תחלתו כל שהוא - משתגמר מלאכתו שיריו ברובו. במשניות גרסינן: "תחלתו כל שהוא, שיריו ברובו, משתגמר מלאכתו, ואיזהו גמר מלאכתו וכו'". ודרך הש"ס שמהפך פעמים מסדר המשנה לפי הצורך, משום דבפ' העור והרוטב (חולין דף קכד.) בעי: "רובו דטפח למאי חזי?", ומשני: אגדול תני ליה בסוף. ופריך: "והא שיריו ד' קאמר?!", ומשני: "לא קשיא, הא בתנור בר ט', הא בתנור בר ז'". ומפרש התם רש"י, דבתנור ט' סגי בארבעה, אע"ג דלא הוי רובא; ותנור ז', אע"ג דלא הוי ד', סגי ברובא. וקשה לר"ת: לא יהיה סופו חמור מתחלתו, דהא תחלתו ד'! ונראה כפירש"י שפירש כאן, דתנור בר ז' — וד' הוי רובא, ותנור בר תשעה — ברובא. וקשה: דלמה ליה למנקט בר ט'? הוה ליה למנקט בר ח' ושיריו ברובו! ולפרש"י דהתם ניחא, דנקט ט', אע"ג דהוי ד' מיעוטא. ומה שהקשה ר"ת — לא קשה מידי, דהעושה כלי חרס אינו עושה אלא דבר חשוב, אבל כלי שנתמעט, כל זמן שראוי אינו מתבטל, כמו גרדומי ציצית דבשירים סגי. וכן משמע מדפריך: "שיריו טפח למאי חזי?" — משמע דאי הוה חזי, הוה ניחא ליה, אע"ג דבציר מתחלתו:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:2:2.english: In its original state, any size - Once its construction is completed, its remains [are impure] with its majority. In the Mishnayot, we read: "In its original state, any size; its remains [are impure] with its majority; once its construction is completed; and what is the completion of its construction, etc." And it is the way of the Talmud to sometimes reverse the order of the Mishnah according to need; [and here it changed the order] because in the chapter HaOr VeHaRotev (Chullin 124a) it asks: "A majority of a handbreadth — what is it fit for?" And it answers: It is taught at the end, referring to the large [oven]. And it asks: "But does it not say that its remains are four [handbreadths]?" And it answers: "There is no difficulty: this refers to an oven of nine [handbreadths], and that refers to an oven of seven [handbreadths]." And Rashi explains there that in a nine-[handbreadth] oven, four [handbreadths] suffice, even though it is not a majority; and in a seven-[handbreadth] oven, even though it is not four [handbreadths], its majority suffices. And Rabbenu Tam raises a difficulty: its end [remains] should not be more stringent [in contracting impurity] than its beginning, for its beginning is four [handbreadths]! And it appears [correct] like Rashi's explanation that he explained here: that [one Mishnah] refers to an oven of seven [handbreadths], where four is its majority; and [the other Mishnah] refers to an oven of nine [handbreadths], [where it is impure] with its majority. Yet it is difficult: why did [the Gemara] need to mention a nine-[handbreadth] oven? It could have mentioned an eight-[handbreadth] oven, where its remains are its majority! Whereas according to Rashi's explanation there, it is understandable why it chose nine — [to teach that four suffices] even though four is a minority. And as for what Rabbenu Tam asked — it is no difficulty at all, for one who makes an earthenware vessel only makes a significant object; however, a vessel that has diminished, as long as it is usable, does not lose its status, like remnants of tzitzit, where remains suffice. And so it is implied from [the Gemara's] asking: "If its remains are a handbreadth, what is it fit for?" — which implies that if it were usable, it would be acceptable to [the Gemara], even though it is smaller than its beginning.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:3:1.hebrew: כל שהוא טפח - פר"ת בלא יחפור (ב"ב דף יט), דפעמים כל שהוא בציר מטפח, ופעמים טפי מטפח:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:3:1.english: Any size — a handbreadth - Rabbeinu Tam explained in [the chapter] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 19) that sometimes "any size" [means] less than a handbreadth, and sometimes more than a handbreadth.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:3:2.hebrew: בפלוגתא לא קמיירי - ואע"ג דפליגי בדופן סוכה, דר"ש אומר דרביעית טפח — מ"מ טפח לדופן אחד צריך לכ"ע. אבל לתנור — אע"ג דבין התנור ולכותל לכ"ע טפח, מ"מ בסתם תנור פליגי. והא דפרש"י דכירה מקום שפיתת קדרה אחת — לא דק, דבפ' כירה (שבת דף לח:) אמר דכירה זהו מקום שפיתת ב' קדרות:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:3:2.english: He is not speaking of [matters subject to] dispute - And even though they disagree regarding the wall of a sukkah, as Rabbi Shimon says [that it need only be] a quarter of a handbreadth — nevertheless, one handbreadth for one wall is required according to everyone. But with respect to an oven — even though [the space] between the oven and the wall is one handbreadth according to everyone, nevertheless they disagree regarding an ordinary oven. And as for that which Rashi explained, that a kirah [stove] is a place for setting one pot — he was imprecise, for in the chapter [entitled] Kirah (Shabbat 38b) [the Gemara] states that a kirah is a place for setting two pots.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:9:1.hebrew: את אמרת שמעתתיה דרב - כלומר, כוונת מעצמך, ומתחלה שכחת, ולכך שתק. ולפ"ה שפי' בתמיה, צריך לומר דמתחלה לא חש להשיבו:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:9:1.english: "You said Rav's teaching" - That is to say: You reasoned [it] out on your own, and at first you forgot, and therefore he was silent. And according to the explanation [of Rashi], who explained [this] as a rhetorical question, one must say that at first he did not bother to answer him.

Tosafot on Niddah 26b:9:2.hebrew: ילדה ואח"כ הפילה שליא אפי' עד י' ימים אין חוששין לולד אחר - אע"ג דאמר לקמן דנשתהא הולד שלשה חדשים, מ"מ לא שכיח, וכל כמה דלא חזינן לא חיישינן:
Tosafot on Niddah 26b:9:2.english: "If she gave birth and subsequently discharged an afterbirth, even up to ten days, we are not concerned for another offspring" - Even though [the Gemara] says below that an offspring was delayed three months, nevertheless [such a thing] is uncommon, and as long as we do not see [another offspring], we are not concerned.
